candidates.statement: • FDA strongly discourages disseminating data from ongoing trials. Knowledge of 206 accumulating data by trial investigators and subjects can adversely affect subject accrual, 207 adherence, and retention, as well as endpoint assessment, compromising the ability of the 208 trial to reliably achieve its objective in a timely manner. Issues with trial conduct caused 209 by knowledge of interim results are difficult to predict and generally impossible to adjust 210 for in statistical analyses. Therefore, releasing interim results could have ramifications on 211 the integrity of the ongoing trial and the ability to collect reliable and interpretable data 212 needed to support regulatory decision-making. If sponsors intend to conduct interim 213 analyses, FDA recommends they prospectively plan these analyses and incorporate 214 processes to maintain the integrity of the trial (e.g., using an independent DMC). 15 FDA 215 recognizes there may be exceptional circumstances in which a sponsor determines it 216 needs to disseminate results for safety or other reasons. In such situations, the sponsor is 217 strongly encouraged to discuss with FDA before releasing such results. 218
